title: KernelProbeRequest
description: The `-Prequest=` input of `./gradlew :adapter:kernelProbe`: one document model plus one or more named documents to observe the REAL kernel's runtime validation over. Relative `model`/`document` references resolve against THIS FILE'S directory, so a request and its inputs form one movable bundle. The probe grows no authoring surface: the model is authored with dmtool's structured verbs (`rule add`, `computation add`, …) and passed here already complete, self-contained, and expanded — it is loaded exactly as the kernel's own deserializer does, with no reference resolution, so an unexpanded model is refused. The normative contract is docs/KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC.md.
$comment: `rows` is conditionally required rather than always: see the allOf at the end, which mirrors the producer's own rule that a per-row observation needs rows and validateFull, and that a model-level-only request needs neither.

model.description: path to the DM-JSON document model, relative to this request file or absolute. A model the kernel's consistency oracle reports an ERROR on is REFUSED with those diagnostics rather than evaluated — an inconsistent model would otherwise observe nothing at all, which reads as 'nothing fired'.

locale.description: the evaluation locale, in A12's `language_COUNTRY` form. It MUST be one the model DECLARES: the kernel refuses any other outright (`Locale 'en_US' is not supported in the document model '…'`, measured 2026-08-11), so a German-only model needs `de_DE` here rather than merely producing English text. Only the `message` channel is locale-dependent; `code`, `type`, `severity`, and every address are not.

clock.description: an ISO-8601 instant pinning the kernel's `currentDateForTest` (both Today and Now) on BOTH strategies. Required for a byte-reproducible artifact whenever any rule reads the current date; omitted, the real clock is used and only clock-independent models reproduce.

customFieldTypes.description: the custom field types this request REGISTERS with the kernel, keyed by the technical type name a `CustomFieldType` field declares. Without it a FILLED custom cell is unobservable rather than merely unvalidated: the kernel resolves a validator from the per-call `DocumentProcessingConfig.customFieldTypeFactory` and falls back to the static `CustomFieldTypeService`, both empty unless a host registers one, and an unresolved type raises `ValidatorException: Custom field validator '<name>' missing.` out of the WHOLE `validateFull` call on both strategies — taking every other rule on that document with it. An empty cell short-circuits before the validator, so a model with custom fields observes cleanly until one is filled. The shape is dmtool's own `--predefined-types` registry, deliberately, rather than a second spelling of one concept; its imperative sibling (`--custom-field-types-js`) is NOT mirrored, because a probe artifact is pinned by SHA-256 and every input must be reproducible from the request bytes alone. OMIT the key to declare nothing — an empty object is refused, because it reads as a default while leaving the cell exactly as unobservable as its absence does.

additionalProperties.description: one declared type. Every constraint is optional and an absent one is unconstrained; the validator applies `pattern`, then these lengths, then the FIELD's own declared `minLength`/`maxLength`, which the kernel hands over through `ICustomFieldTypeValidationParam` — a CUSTOM field's declared bounds are enforced by nobody else (KERNEL-FINDINGS KF54), so a registry that ignores them makes them advisory. Each failure names the constraint that produced it in the message `code` (`customFieldType.pattern`, `customFieldType.minLength`, `field.maxLength`, …), which is A12's own rule that the code is the validator's `getErrorKey()` rather than a fixed kernel code.

pattern.description: a java.util.regex pattern the WHOLE value must match; an unparseable one is refused at request-read time rather than at the first row

items.description: a kernel entry point, named as the kernel names the method. Three are PER-ROW: `validateFull` produces each engine block's `messages`, `compute` its `computations`, `validatePart` its `partialMessages`. Two are PER-MODEL: `mandatoryInformation` (`IRuleCollectionMetaInformation.getMandatoryInformationFromRules`) reads the model's rule conditions, needs no document, and produces the top-level `mandatoryInformation` block once for the request. `dynamicEnumerations` (`IRuleCollectionMetaInformation.getDynamicEnumerationStringValues`) is the same shape and the ONLY route to the kernel's dynamic-enumeration derivation — its checker has exactly one caller in the kernel, so `checkConsistency` never reaches its twelve MVK_DYNENUM_* classes. Its diagnostics are NOT defects: the derivation checks every rule and reports one problem per rule that is not a dynamic enumeration in form, which is true of almost every ordinary rule. `validatePart` additionally requires every row to carry `relevant`, because a partial validation with no declared coverage would silently be a full one.

observe.description: which kernel entry points to observe. OMIT IT for validation alone — that is the default, and a request without this key produces a BYTE-IDENTICAL artifact to the one it produced before `compute` was observable, so an already-pinned SHA-256 stays valid. `validateFull` may not be dropped WHENEVER ANY ROW IS OBSERVED: an engine block's `messages` is a REQUIRED key of schemaVersion 1, so a list left empty because nobody looked would be indistinguishable from one where nothing fired. (`computations` avoids that ambiguity by being absent when unobserved; `messages` was not given the same treatment because making a required key optional changes the shape of artifacts consumers already pin. The refusal is therefore a compatibility decision, and it costs a compute-only consumer a validation pass per row per strategy.) A request naming ONLY model-level observations observes no row, so it neither needs nor accepts `rows`, and `validateFull` does not apply. Duplicates are accepted — this is a set. An explicit empty array is refused: omitting the key means the default, writing `[]` means a mistake.

rows.description: the ordered observations. Each row's document is evaluated on every kernel strategy; the artifact keeps the row order. REQUIRED whenever `observe` names a per-row entry point, and REFUSED when it names only model-level ones — a row nothing looks at is the same silent no-op the `validateFull` rule refuses.

name.description: this observation's identity in the artifact; must be unique within the request

document.description: path to an A12 canonical Document JSON instance, relative to this request file or absolute — the same shape `dmtool model seed` writes and `model eval --instance` reads (schema `document-instance.schema.json`), so one document file feeds both the interpreter and this probe. Exactly one of `document` / `documentInline` is required.

documentInline.description: the A12 canonical Document JSON embedded directly, for a self-contained single-file request. Exactly one of `document` / `documentInline` is required.

relevant.description: this row's CALLER-SUPPLIED relevant set for `validatePart` — required exactly when `observe` names it, and refused otherwise (a key nothing reads). An EMPTY array is not an omission: it is the kernel's `noneRelevant` coverage, one of the two shapes `validateFull` cannot express. A relevant group makes all its descendants relevant.

path.description: the model path of the relevant element, e.g. /Order/Lines/Amount

reps.description: the 1-based repetition index of each part of `path`, in order — ONE PER PATH PART, not per repeatable part. The kernel refuses a mismatch outright (`fullName and repetition have different length`), so `/Order/Lines/Amount` needs three entries even when only `Lines` repeats. `0` is the kernel's own wildcard (`IEntityInstance.ALL_SEMANTIC`) meaning every repetition of that element. OMIT the key for the all-wildcard coverage of the right length, which is what almost every consumer wants and removes the need to count parts by hand.

allOf.$comment: no `observe` means the default ['validateFull'], which is per-row
any per-row observation requires both `rows` and `validateFull`
only model-level observations read no document, so a row would be observed by nothing
validatePart needs a declared coverage per row; without one it would silently be validateFull
…and a relevant set nothing reads is the same silent no-op the rules above refuse
